Summary

Transport pods, shuttles, and modded transporter-like things with cargo (anything with a CompTransporter, never coupled to CompShuttle) gain:

- "Bulk unload all" toggle on the gizmo row (icon: vanilla's Set-to-load art flipped, shipped as Interface/BulkUnloadAll.png). While on, hauling colonists empty the hold one backpack-filling trip at a time, several pawns in parallel, until nothing pullable remains, then the flag self-clears.
- Right-click "Prioritize bulk unloading" order, visible only while the toggle is on. Ordering does not touch the flag; it makes that pawn prioritize the shuttle over other work (the driver chains follow-up visits behind each storage drop-off). Autonomous trips respect forbiddance; ordered trips take everything.
- Mutual exclusion, both directions: a flagged hold greys out vanilla's "Set to load" and refuses HD load jobs (both HasPotentialBulkWork and TryGiveBulkJob, lockstep); a load owning the hold greys the toggle and the order, and yields any visit in flight. Load sessions are tracked explicitly (birth: InitiateLoading/TryAccept, both branches; death: TryRemoveLord/CancelLoad), because vanilla's InitiateLoading only stamps group IDs and pure-cargo loads never grow a lord. A slow-tick janitor is the backstop; every player-action path clears state synchronously.

Design notes

- Pull ladder is the shared CorpseSweepPolicy-aware carrier logic: backpack-first by free mass, overflow to hands, CE weight/bulk clamp, PlanHandsFallback when CE is exhausted (no massless-stack re-plan leak). Corpses follow bulkHaulCorpses + the disposal-only auto-strip carve-out; corpses never ride in backpacks when the opt-in is off.
- Pawns in a hold are never pulled; pawns-only return-trip drains (ShipJob_Unload) are exempt from the conflict gate since they never touch cargo.
- No reservation on the transporter (mirrors the load side); concurrent pulls are safe via single-threaded toils plus per-pull Contains/count clamps.
- VF vehicles excluded at all entry points; no Rand in gates; all scribed-state writes happen on deterministic in-tick paths or through the MP-synced SetBulkUnloadAll.

Changeset
- minor, recorded in .changeset/feat-bulk-unload-shuttles.md

tested in game:
-various permutations of landing/not landing, starting loading/partial loading/stopping loading, starting unloading/partial unloading/stopping unloading
-smoke tested a quest shuttle
-performance appears fine when testing with 16k corn, vanilla's "dump all cargo on floor" button + bulk hauling causes flickering drops to 100tps, bulk unloading a shuttle doesnt have the same obvious tps drops

actionable:
-prioritize bulk unloading is chained repeatedly until drained not only done once like prioritize bulk load. we should pick one or the other for consistency
-new translations should be ran again through the same LLM/workflow as others, at least in Polish the new translations use a different case so they are correct but out of place with existing
-~130 shared lines between the carrier and transporter unload drivers

not tested:
multiplayer (i saw awareness during work)
HD's own compatibility with other mods (i saw CE awareness during work but this should be reviewed by someone more familiar)

When ordering a pawn to "haul everything", the pawn reserves all items lying nearby. If you send another pawn to haul any reserved item, the first pawn cancels all of the "haul everything" work.

If the pawn did not reserve all nearby items at the moment of the order, but after picking up the first item looked for the next one and then continued - then multiple pawns would be able to work.

sources.body:
## Problem

Loading a save produced an instant, colony-wide freeze: every pawn stood still with a job visible in the inspect pane but never moved. The log showed a NullReferenceException storm — `Exception ticking <pawn> … Suppressing further errors` for one colonist after another, with the NRE surfacing in `Pawn_JobTracker.TryOpportunisticJob`, `Pawn_JobTracker.EndCurrentJob`, and `WorkGiver_HaulGeneral.JobOnThing` → `HaulAIUtility.PawnCanAutomaticallyHaulFast_NewTemp`.

Root cause (diagnosed from the live save + 1.6.4871 decompile): a bill-syncing mod (WorkbenchConnect's `WorkbenchGroupManager` map component) deep-saves **live** `Bill_ProductionWithUft` objects inside its own `<savedBills>`. `Bill.billStack` is `[Unsaved]`, so after a load such a bill exists with a **null stack** — while its `boundUft` cross-reference still binds it to a real `UnfinishedThing` on the map (the UFT's own `bill` ref resolves right back to the stashed copy). Every haul-candidate check then reads `uft.BoundBill`, whose getter validates `Bill.DeletedOrDereferenced`, which dereferences `billStack.billGiver` → NRE. Since the bound UFT sits in `listerHaulables`, **every pawn that finishes any job** (opportunistic-haul probe) and every hauling work scan hits it; RimWorld freezes each crashing pawn's ticking. Mid-session the stashed bill still holds a stale non-null `billStack` pointer, which is why the session that wrote the save ran fine and the explosion only starts on the next load.

## Fix

Two layers, mirroring the existing null-def-job guard pair (`Patch_Pawn_JobTracker_EndCurrentJob_NullDefGuard` + `RepairOrphanedJobsAfterLoad`):

- **`UnfinishedThing.ExposeData` prefix** — at `PostLoadInit`, unbind a UFT from a bound bill whose `billStack == null` (covers every scribed UFT: spawned, pawn inventory, caravan). At `Saving`, the same unbind protects vanilla's own pre-save `DeletedOrDereferenced` read, which would otherwise NRE and abort the save. Raw field access on both sides — the `BoundBill` getter is the code that crashes on this state, so it is never invoked.
- **`FinalizeInit` backstop sweep** over `ThingRequestGroup.HaulableEver` (exactly the set the crashing scans iterate) for modded UFT subclasses whose `ExposeData` override skips `base`; emits one aggregated repair message.

The unbind is non-destructive: the UFT keeps its ingredients/work and becomes an ordinary loose unfinished item that a matching bench bill re-adopts; the foreign component's stored bill object is otherwise untouched. A missing/renamed `boundBillInt` field can only *disable* the guard (no-throw binding + `Prepare()` gate inside the per-class patch isolation), never abort a scribe pass.

## Verification

- `bun run build` clean (0 errors), `bun run test` 2080/2080 pass.
- Adversarial multi-agent review against the 1.6.4871 decompile (patch mechanics / false-positive unbinding / coverage): no false-positive scenario is constructible from vanilla semantics — `billStack` is assigned in `BillStack.AddBill` and the `BillStack.ExposeData` load restore, never nulled, and vanilla's only UFT-bind sites use on-stack bills; bill clones/clipboard never carry `boundUftInt`. Coverage confirmed: cross-refs resolve before `PostLoadInit`, and the sweep runs before the first tick.
- In-game repro pending (needs the corrupted save): loading the affected save with this build should print `[Hauler's Dream] Save repair: unbound N unfinished thing(s) …` once and pawns should work normally. Will confirm on the live save before undrafting.

Known sibling (deliberately not handled): the same duplicated-bill state can reach a pawn saved mid-DoBill via `Job.bill`; that path NREs once inside `JobDriver` fail-condition checking, is caught by its error recovery, and self-heals — a one-time red log line, not a freeze.
